opportunities.title: Undergraduate Research Assistant — Power Transformation Lab
opportunities.eligibility: Undergraduate students · Python or Julia proficiency
opportunities.description: The Power Transformation Lab is hiring multiple undergraduate research assistants for projects running October 2026 – June 2027, covering data extraction and visualization, statistical analysis, and independent research on macro energy systems.
opportunities.responsibilities: Extract and scrape data from documents and websites; build data visualizations; perform basic statistical analysis; contribute to independent research projects.
opportunities.requirements: Cover letter describing your interests and relevant experience; resume. Proficiency in Python or Julia required. GIS, database, or AI-tool experience is a plus.
opportunities.process: Apply through the Handshake job posting (ID 11459763) and follow the instructions listed there.
opportunities.funding: Paid hourly position — see Handshake posting for details
opportunities.keywords: energy research assistant python julia data visualization handshake

opportunities.title: Cal-in-Sacramento Fellowship
opportunities.org: Matsui Center for Politics and Public Service
opportunities.eligibility: UC Berkeley undergraduates passionate about public service
opportunities.description: One of UC's largest campus-based public service programs. Fellows take a 3-unit spring course on California policy and politics plus professional development and research training, then complete an eight-week summer internship in Sacramento — in Senate and Assembly offices, the Governor's Office, state agencies, think tanks, or nonprofits. 25–30 fellows selected each year.
opportunities.responsibilities: Spring coursework and research training; full-time summer public-service internship with a Sacramento host office.
opportunities.requirements: Online application; see program page for full requirements and eligibility details.
opportunities.process: Apply via the Matsui Center's 2026–27 program application page before the deadline.
opportunities.funding: Free shared housing in Sacramento + transportation and living stipend
opportunities.keywords: public service internship sacramento policy politics fellowship

opportunities.title: Undergraduate Research Apprentice Program (URAP) — Spring 2027
opportunities.deadlineNote: Representative date — applications open for a two-week window after the first day of the spring semester
opportunities.description: Work directly with faculty and research staff on cutting-edge projects across every school and college at Berkeley. Apprentices deepen their knowledge in an area of special interest while experiencing life in a research community.
opportunities.responsibilities: Varies by project — lab work, data analysis, fieldwork, literature review, participant recruitment, and more.
opportunities.requirements: Online application via the URAP portal, including a statement of interest and research-relevant coursework.
opportunities.process: Browse spring projects on the URAP portal when the application window opens; interview with mentors; file a Learning Contract if selected.
opportunities.funding: Academic credit — 1 unit per 3 hours of research per week (up to 4 units/term)
opportunities.keywords: urap apprentice faculty mentor research credit

opportunities.title: SUPERB 2027 — Summer Undergraduate Program in Engineering Research at Berkeley (AI4E)
opportunities.org: Dept. of Electrical Engineering & Computer Sciences (EECS)
opportunities.deadlineNote: Representative date — based on the prior cycle's late-January deadline
opportunities.eligibility: Undergraduates · juniors/seniors preferred · interest in AI for Engineering
opportunities.description: A 9-week summer REU site (June–August) focused on Artificial Intelligence for Engineering: machine learning algorithms, safety in human-robot interaction, provably-safe AI systems, adversarial robustness, and engineering design influenced by large language models.
opportunities.responsibilities: Full-time summer research project with an EECS faculty mentor and graduate students; weekly presentations; lab tours; industry field trip; graduate-school advising.
opportunities.requirements: Online application; personal statement demonstrating interest in the research theme.
opportunities.process: Apply through the SUPERB program page; decisions typically announced in spring.

opportunities.keywords: superb reu summer engineering ai machine learning stipend housing

opportunities.title: SURF L&S — Summer Undergraduate Research Fellowship 2027
opportunities.deadlineNote: Representative date — based on the prior cycle's mid-March deadline
opportunities.eligibility: L&S undergraduates with junior/senior standing · 3.0+ GPA · faculty mentor required
opportunities.description: Seven weeks of full-time, faculty-mentored summer research on an independent project of your own design — culminating in a senior thesis or other capstone project. Includes a research cluster community, workshops, and the SURF Conference in August.
opportunities.responsibilities: Design and execute an original summer research project full-time for at least seven weeks; present at the SURF Conference.
opportunities.requirements: Well-written research proposal; committed UC Berkeley faculty mentor; attend an application workshop or advising consultation before applying.
opportunities.process: Submit the online application with proposal and mentor commitment; see the SURF page for the current cycle's instructions.
opportunities.keywords: surf fellowship summer independent research thesis capstone

opportunities.title: Haas Scholars Program 2026–27
opportunities.deadlineNote: Representative date — confirm on the official page
opportunities.eligibility: Seniors graduating Fall 2026 or Spring/Summer 2027 · 3.450+ GPA · eligible for need-based financial aid
opportunities.description: A year-long funded senior capstone for 20 scholars selected across the humanities, STEM, and social sciences. Close mentoring from UC Berkeley faculty, interdisciplinary cohort seminars and workshops, and a professional conference presentation.
opportunities.responsibilities: Carry out an original, feasible senior research or creative project (~10 hrs/week); participate in cohort events throughout the year.

opportunities.process: Apply online when the application opens in early fall; applications are read by discipline-based selection committees.

opportunities.org: College of Computing, Data Science, and Society (CDSS)
opportunities.deadlineNote: Applications posted before the start of each semester
opportunities.eligibility: UC Berkeley undergraduates · all majors welcome
opportunities.description: Semester-long, team-based data science projects with industry, government, nonprofit, and academic partners. opportunities.title: DOE SULI Internship — Summer 2027 (Berkeley Lab)
opportunities.org: U.S. Department of Energy — Science Undergraduate Laboratory Internships (SULI)
opportunities.eligibility: Full-time students at four-year institutions and community colleges, and recent graduates within two years of receiving a bachelor's or associate degree
opportunities.description: SULI places undergraduates in paid 10-week summer research internships at DOE national laboratories — including Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, just above the UC Berkeley campus. Interns work with scientists, engineers, and technical professionals on real research projects supporting the DOE mission, from quantum information science and fusion to biotechnology, critical minerals, advanced manufacturing, and cybersecurity. Applications for the Summer 2027 term are open now.
opportunities.responsibilities: Conduct a mentored research or technical project with a host-lab team; participate in lab seminars and professional development; present your work at the end of the term.
opportunities.requirements: Online application through the DOE WDTS portal, including research interests, preferred laboratory choices (select Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory), and letters of recommendation; see the WDTS SULI page for full eligibility rules.
opportunities.process: Apply on the DOE WDTS SULI portal by January 6, 2027, 5:00 p.m. ET. Free application workshops run Nov 4, 2026, an alumni panel Dec 8, 2026, and a virtual internship fair Nov 12, 2026.
opportunities.funding: Paid stipend; participants living outside the commuting area also receive round-trip travel and lodging assistance
opportunities.location: Berkeley, CA · Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory
opportunities.sourceName: DOE Office of Science — SULI program page
opportunities.keywords: suli doe berkeley lab lbnl national laboratory summer internship paid stem

opportunities.title: Charles H. Percy Undergraduate Grant for Public Affairs Research
opportunities.eligibility: Registered UC Berkeley undergraduate students conducting original research on an aspect of American politics
opportunities.description: IGS awards up to four $1,000 research grants each year to UC Berkeley undergraduates conducting original research on American politics — including public opinion, electoral behavior, civic participation, government institutions, social movements, and public policy. Students from a broad range of disciplines are encouraged to apply. The current application cycle closes November 29, 2026.
opportunities.responsibilities: Carry out your proposed research project; recipients are invited to present their research at the Percy Synar Award Ceremony and Reception at IGS (February 26, 2027).
opportunities.requirements: Brief questionnaire, essay, budget and brief description of research expenses, resume, and transcript(s); one recommendation from a UC Berkeley faculty member or GSI, due by the same deadline.
opportunities.process: Apply via the IGS Percy Grant application page by Sunday, November 29, 2026, 11:59 p.m. Recipients are notified in mid-December 2026 and awards are issued in January 2027.
opportunities.funding: $1,000 research grant (up to four awarded annually)
opportunities.keywords: percy grant igs politics public affairs research funding american politics $1000

opportunities.title: Amgen Scholars Program at UC Berkeley — Summer 2027
opportunities.org: Amgen Scholars Program at UC Berkeley
opportunities.deadlineNote: Amgen Scholars' common application deadline — the portal opens November 1, 2026; confirm Berkeley-specific details on the Amgen application portal
opportunities.eligibility: Undergraduates enrolled in accredited four-year colleges or universities in the U.S. (any institution, not just Berkeley); GPA 3.2 or higher; sophomores, juniors, or non-graduating seniors; U.S. citizens or permanent residents; interest in pursuing a PhD or MD-PhD
opportunities.description: Amgen Scholars at UC Berkeley spend ten weeks of intensive, full-time research in a Berkeley faculty laboratory, working directly with an in-lab mentor (a postdoc or graduate student) in fields such as biological sciences, bioengineering, biophysics, chemical and biomolecular engineering, chemistry, chemical biology, and computational biology. The program adds weekly faculty seminars, workshops on scientific writing, careers, and graduate admissions, and the Amgen Scholars North America Symposium in July.
opportunities.responsibilities: Full-time laboratory research on a faculty-mentored project; weekly lab meetings and journal clubs; faculty seminars and professional development workshops; poster and oral presentations at the end of the summer.
opportunities.requirements: Online application through the Amgen Scholars portal (opens November 1, 2026), including transcripts, a personal statement, and letters of recommendation, per the portal instructions.
opportunities.process: Apply through the central Amgen Scholars application by February 1, 2027; each host institution reviews its own applicants.
opportunities.funding: Stipend, coverage of summer session fees, campus apartment housing, meal allowance, round-trip travel to Berkeley, and the North America Symposium
opportunities.sourceName: Amgen Scholars — UC Berkeley host institution page
opportunities.keywords: amgen scholars summer research biotechnology biology chemistry bioengineering stipend phd

opportunities.title: UC LEADS Research Program (via Cal NERDS)
opportunities.org: Cal NERDS — New Experiences for Research and Diversity in Science
opportunities.deadlineNote: Applications for the 2027 cohort open January 2027; five to seven scholars are selected each spring — check the Cal NERDS page for the closing date
opportunities.eligibility: Registered UC Berkeley STEM students who have experienced situations or conditions that adversely impacted their advancement; at least one semester completed at Berkeley; U.S. citizens, permanent residents, or DREAMers; ideally ~3.0 GPA; designed for sophomores and juniors (transfer juniors welcome)
opportunities.description: UC LEADS is a UC-wide, typically two-year program that prepares promising STEM undergraduates for doctoral study through paid summer research, leadership and professional development, advising, community building, and graduate school application support. Scholars do a paid summer research internship at UC Berkeley and often a second paid summer at another UC campus; 76% of UC LEADS research scholars go on to STEM graduate programs.
opportunities.responsibilities: Eight weeks of faculty-mentored summer research (35 hrs/week in the lab plus 5 hrs/week of workshops, mid-June to early August); poster presentations at the end of summer and at the statewide UC LEADS symposium; a two-year (two-summer) commitment for sophomores.
opportunities.requirements: Application through Cal NERDS when the cohort window opens (January 2027 for the 2027 cohort); see the program page for the application components.
opportunities.process: Apply via the Cal NERDS UC LEADS page; five to seven scholars are selected each spring.
opportunities.funding: Paid summer research — stipend typically $4,500 per summer, plus help with housing, food, and transportation for the host-campus summer
opportunities.location: Berkeley, CA · second summer often at another UC campus
opportunities.sourceName: Cal NERDS — UC LEADS program page
opportunities.keywords: uc leads cal nerds paid summer research stem diversity phd preparation first-generation

opportunities.title: Break into Biotech (QB3)
opportunities.org: QB3 — California Institute for Quantitative Biosciences
opportunities.deadlineNote: Applications opened Friday, September 4, 2026; no closing deadline is posted on the program page — the training cohort starts in February, so apply early
opportunities.eligibility: UC Berkeley students who aspire to work in labs but face financial constraints and/or a lack of experience; applicants should have responsibilities to support the financial costs of their education
opportunities.description: Break into Biotech bridges the gap for UC Berkeley students who want lab careers but lack experience or can't afford unpaid training. A 5-week paid training program builds essential benchwork skills; graduates are then matched into paid academic research in UC Berkeley labs for spring through summer, and fully trained candidates can apply for 6-month paid internships at Bakar Bio Labs tenant startups and other companies through the partner QWEST program. Everything is paid — the program states 'we pay you to train.'
opportunities.responsibilities: Hands-on bench-skills training (~5 hours/week for 5 weeks starting early February); then a paid research placement in a UC Berkeley lab; optional application to 6-month startup internships.
opportunities.requirements: Online application via the QB3 Break into Biotech page; selection is aimed at students with financial need and little prior lab experience.
opportunities.process: Apply on the QB3 website (applications opened September 4, 2026). Training begins in February; lab matches follow for spring–summer.
opportunities.funding: Fully funded — paid training, paid lab research placement, and paid internship pathway; no financial burden on students
opportunities.location: Berkeley, CA · QB3 / Bakar Bio Labs
opportunities.sourceName: QB3 — Break into Biotech program page
opportunities.keywords: qb3 break into biotech paid training benchwork bakar bio labs internship startup

opportunities.title: Biology Scholars Program (BSP)
opportunities.deadlineNote: No single annual deadline is posted — membership admission runs through BSP and its research placements are for members; check the BSP apply page for the current window
opportunities.eligibility: UC Berkeley undergraduates in the biological sciences — BSP has served 3,800+ students, primarily from low-income, first-generation, and minoritized backgrounds
opportunities.description: BSP is a long-running Berkeley community that helps biology undergraduates — especially low-income, first-in-family, and minoritized students — succeed in science, pairing advising, peer community, and study support with real research pathways. Through its Program for Early Researchers (PER), members with little or no experience are matched into campus research labs; through the Research Fellows Program (RFP), members already in a lab can receive research stipends so financial need doesn't force them into unpaid work.
opportunities.responsibilities: Active membership: new-student orientation, an introductory advising meeting, the IB C96 (fall) and MCB 15 (spring) courses in the first two years, and contributing to the BSP community; research placements through PER/RFP as matched.
opportunities.requirements: Apply for BSP membership via the BSP apply page; PER is for current members with little/no prior research experience, RFP for members already placed in a research group.
opportunities.process: Apply to BSP on its website; once a member, apply to PER for a lab match or to RFP for a research stipend.
opportunities.funding: Advising, community, and coursework support for all members; research stipends available to members through the Research Fellows Program
opportunities.location: Berkeley, CA · Valley Life Sciences Building
opportunities.sourceName: Biology Scholars Program — Apply to BSP
opportunities.keywords: bsp biology scholars program first-generation low-income research placement stipend mcb ib
